But we can assume we are in some directory. We need to navigate to temp directory. In typical Unix, temp directory is /tmp. But we don't have a tool to change directory. We can just list /tmp? But ls tool only lists current directory. There's no tool to change directory. We might need to use find with path? find can search from a path. But listing all files in /tmp including hidden? find can list all items. But they want to list all files in that directory. We can use find with path="/tmp" and name=None. That will list all files and directories recursively. But they want to list all available files in that directory. Could use ls with a? But ls only lists current directory. We can't change directory. So we can use find to list all items in /tmp. But that includes subdirectories. They might want just top-level. We can use find with max depth? There's no max depth param. But we can filter by pattern? Not exactly. We could use ls -a on /tmp? But ls doesn't accept path. So we can't. We can use find to list all items in /tmp. That will include hidden ones. So let's do find with path="/tmp" and name=None.
